rules.sentence: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy are 2 conditions that can cause cardiac syncope, recognizable by specific histopathologic findings.

The classic findings on myocardial biopsy of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy include a thickened myocardium (often specifically in the septum), disorganization of myocyte fibers, myocardial scarring and fibrosis, as well as narrowed vessels and dysplasia of the tunica media cells.
